trickyParts: A DPoP proof is single use by its jti and htu, so a request's presentation is decided once per request (decideBrokerToken) and carried on the request: a route that resolves its caller twice (requireAuthenticated then requireActor, or a keyed write) would otherwise present one proof twice and refuse the second as the replay it would be. An open stream's fifteen-second re-resolution reads the token's liveness alone (Verifier.Live) for the same reason.

htu is checked against DISPATCH_SERVER_URL plus the request's path, never X-Forwarded-Proto or r.Host, which a caller behind the deployment's proxy could choose. atOrigin rewrites the request exactly as the broker's own atPublicURL does.

brokertoken.Presented reads the Authorization header itself rather than calling rfc9449.AccessTokenFromRequest: that helper falls through to oauth2.AccessTokenFromRequest, which calls ParseMultipartForm and would eat the body of every multipart upload that is not this credential. The suite has a row for it.

The per-source-address bucket is spent inside the single flight, so one request of the bucket buys exactly one introspection: charging per request would refuse an honest caller that made a burst of calls on a token it had just been given, and TestRequestsArrivingAtOnceWithOneTokenCostOneIntrospection pins it with a bucket of one.

The project check runs in one wrapper before the handler rather than in seventy handlers. That is sound because nothing moves an object between projects (no `update … set project_key` outside the migrations; a parent and a rank neighbour outside the issue's project are refused rather than moved), and it is a no-op for every credential that names no project.

Revoking an access token sets RevokeRefreshTokensExplicit, so it no longer drags the refresh family's launcher credential down with it: without that, revoking one of a dev box session's access tokens would have logged that machine out entirely under a reuse-detection audit record.

The Postgres this pod runs has C as its default collation and no password-bearing role, and gVisor answers SO_PEERPIDFD 'protocol not available'. Four suites fail for the pod and not the branch: internal/dispatch/api's TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves, internal/broker/store's TestOpenSignsEveryNewConnectionInWithAFreshlyMintedToken, internal/broker/helper and cmd/agent-secrets*. Playwright's webkit and firefox cannot be installed here at all (missing gtk-4, gstreamer and flite); chromium can.

The harness lives at /legion/harness: `bash /legion/harness/setup.sh dispatch_test broker_test dispatch_live dispatch_e2e` rebuilds the unpacked Postgres 17 with pgvector and prints its port, and /legion/harness/env.sh exports DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL and BROKER_TEST_DATABASE_URL. `bun install` and `cd packages/contracts && bun run build` are needed before internal/dispatch/pmdoc and the browser suite will run.
deviations: The architect's point 4 (dispatch://INFRA-264/comment/f968ddb6) replaced the plan's P14: this change adds POST /v1/oauth/revoke, the library's RFC 7009 revocation, so an exchanged access token can be revoked at all, and the revocation line is proven on an exchanged token rather than on a dev box session's. The route is accountAuth with the relaysDecisions power, since ending one of the broker's tokens is the same authority as ending a machine login or a grant, and a caller listed only to read a token back must not hold it.
The plan's P9 named the powers but not their number: there are two, readsTokensBack and relaysDecisions, declared on each accountAuth row, with dispatch holding both and listener holding the first.

The plan's T11 asked for the write class on each route row. Go fills no field of a positional composite literal by default, so a sixth column would make all 146 rows fail to compile; the class is declared in one writeClasses table beside the rows instead, and correspondence is enforced both ways (a mutating row with no class fails its test and refuses the mount; a class naming no served row fails the test).

INFRA-382's real-pod relaunch line stays with dispatch://INFRA-267, as the architect ruled; this change proves it at the broker's own surface, where a relaunch is a second pod uid of the same account.

The pull request was CONFLICTING with main, so GitHub started no workflow run for it and nothing static had ever judged the change. main had moved 62 commits past the fork point: this round merges the base forward (one merge commit, nothing rewritten), resolves the two text conflicts in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and cmd/dispatch/README.md, renumbers the Dispatch migration 0139_dpop_proofs to 0148_dpop_proofs because main now has 0139 through 0147, and gives POST /api/v1/projects/{key}/related - a mutating route main added - its write class, which TestEveryMutatingRouteIsClassed refused the merge without.

That also closes the existence oracle the open behaviour had, where such a caller got 403 for another project's object and 404 for an id nobody holds. TestAnUnknownTargetKeepsTheHandlersAnswer, which pinned the open rule, is rewritten as TestATargetThatResolvesToNoProjectIsRefusedToAProjectScopedToken rather than deleted, and keeps the old assertion for every caller that names no project.

Every one of the fourteen proofs was re-driven live at that head after the merge, against a real broker and a real Dispatch, including both reviews' findings.
openQuestions: The deployment must set BROKER_EXCHANGE_K8S_AUDIENCE, BROKER_EXCHANGE_ACCOUNTS, BROKER_EXCHANGE_WORKFLOWS and BROKER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECONDS, and list Dispatch as the introspection caller, before any pod presents a broker token: dispatch://INFRA-748 owns that and waits on this issue. Nothing here needs them; the live proof runs on scripts/dev-broker.sh, which sets them itself. Do not rename one of those settings after this merges without telling INFRA-748.

BROKER_SERVICE_LOGINS now carries a second authority: an account on it can register any pod of any account the exchange serves. operate.md says so. Narrowing the registrar to its own project's pods needs per-project daemon accounts, which dispatch://INFRA-321 is.

POST /api/v1/messages/{id}/deliveries/{attempt}/accept and POST /api/v1/messages/{id}/reply are classed as the calling session's writes, not a project's, so a session sent a message on another project's issue may reply there. That is the class the route has, and the PR body's Change section now states it rather than leaving the project rule sounding absolute.
discoveredComplexity: The library offers a credential-less caller no path at the revocation endpoint either (the exchange client is registered confidential so the library will grant it the exchange at all), so clientauth.go's existing credential-less branch had to be extended to the revocation endpoint, asserting on the endpoint strategy the library itself picked rather than guessing from the form.

go-oidc formats a KeySet's error with %v, so no sentinel survives IDTokenVerifier.Verify. The adapter carries its key source's error back on the context, which is what lets a key-set outage be reported as ErrIssuerUnavailable rather than as a forged signature.

The Dispatch pool's lease budget has no headroom (store/pool.go says the next leased loop would be a thirteenth caller waiting for a connection), so the DPoP replay sweep runs in the existing leased maintenance pass rather than in a loop of its own.
